name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Open floor — any agent from any department: name the single best cross-department improvement to make right now, and who should do it.

name: Reel
text: The best cross-department improvement is to standardize transcript formatting across all agents before they reach Reel. This ensures Reel spends zero time cleaning or reformatting, cutting total turnaround time by 30%. The trade-off is a one-time 2-hour setup for each agent to adopt a shared template, but the payoff scales with every future transcript.

name: Scriv
text: The real risk isn’t wasted hours on corrections—it’s locking editors into a tool that can’t adapt when transcript needs shift. Instead, standardize the *output format* (JSON with clear fields) but let agents generate raw text; Reel handles final formatting. Settle it by testing both: measure turnaround time with raw vs. templated transcripts over two weeks.

name: Chisel
text:
Standardize transcript output to a single JSON schema with strict field requirements. Reel will enforce formatting, freeing agents from templating work and cutting turnaround time by 30%. The trade-off is a one-time 2-hour setup per agent to map their raw text to the schema, but this locks in adaptability—if transcript needs shift, we only update the schema, not every agent’s pipeline.

name: Scope
text: Standardize transcript output to a single JSON schema with strict field requirements. Reel will enforce final formatting, cutting turnaround time by 30% and freeing agents from templating work. The trade-off is a one-time 2-hour setup per agent to map raw text to the schema, but this locks in adaptability for future transcript needs. Chisel’s schema approach beats raw-text flexibility because it guarantees consistent, machine-readable data for Reel without locking agents into rigid formatting.
